name: King of Makkedah
overview: The King of Makkedah was a male ruler identified as one of the thirty-one kings defeated by Joshua during the conquest of Canaan. His tribal affiliation and family background are not specified in Scripture. He is noted primarily for his defeat, which is recorded in the book of Joshua.
namesAndTitles: This figure is known simply by the title 'King of Makkedah,' which directly denotes his rulership over the city of Makkedah. The name carries no additional given meaning beyond this straightforward designation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships or associations for the King of Makkedah beyond what is noted in his defeat by Joshua. No further personal connections are documented.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Makkedah holds significance as a representative of the Canaanite kings whose defeat marked the fulfillment of God's promise to Israel through Joshua. His conquest symbolizes God's sovereign hand in establishing Israel's possession of the land, demonstrating divine judgment against the inhabitants opposing God's people.
